title: Annotatio VI §.III open: If Lutherans dropped acerbic mode or swapped damnations for bare rejections
pass_a_gloss: §. III. If the Lutherans still so named would today bid this more acerbic mode of treating Controversies to depart, or at least would commute their Damnations — not unlike the Tridentine Anathematisms — into bare Rejections of opinions that seem false to them, though those opinions may, by their own account, perish sometime, yet the Authors and Favorers of them (as being, if at all, certainly erring in good faith) are maximally to be saved and Spiritual Fraternity is to be cultivated with them,
pass_b_english: §. III. If today’s named Lutherans would drop this harsher way of handling controversies — or at least trade their damnations (not unlike Tridentine anathematisms) for bare rejections of opinions they judge false —

then even if those opinions may perish on their own view, the authors and favorers of them (erring, if at all, in good faith) are above all to be saved, and spiritual fraternity is to be kept with them.
source_text:
§. III.
Acerbiorem hunc Controversias tractandi modum si facessere juberent hodieque nominati Lutherani, vel saltem Damnationes suas, Anathematismis Tridentinis haud absimiles, in Rejectiones nudas falsarum sibi ita visarum Opinionum commutarent, quibus licèt, juxta se, perituris aliquando, Autores tamen Fautoresque earum (utpote, si omnino, certè bonâ fide errantes) salvandi sint maximè & cum his Fraternitatem Spiritualem colendi,
notes: §.III open; drop acerbic mode / damnations→bare rejections; save erring authors.
